candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a least common denominator (LCD/LCM) and rewrite one or both fractions as equivalent fractions with that common denominator before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the same operation: determining an LCD/LCM for denominators and converting to equivalent fractions with a shared denominator as a prerequisite to subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Once denominators match, subtract the numerators and keep the common denominator (including results of 0 or negative fractions).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Each codebook includes a skill for executing the actual fraction subtraction with like denominators (numerator subtraction over a fixed denominator), explicitly allowing 0/negative intermediate results.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite mixed numbers or whole numbers into a form suitable for subtraction, such as converting mixed to improper or expressing a whole number as a mixed number with 0 fractional part or as an equivalent fraction with a chosen denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include a representation-change skill covering mixed-to-improper conversion and rewriting whole numbers into compatible fractional/mixed forms; exclusions consistently separate this from LCD-finding and from borrowing/regrouping.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: When needed, borrow/regroup between whole and fractional parts to avoid a negative fractional part, then express the final answer in simplest appropriate form (reduce and/or convert between improper fractions, mixed numbers, and integers).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts combine (1) borrowing/regrouping in mixed-number subtraction when the fractional part would be negative and (2) final-form simplification/conversion (reduce, convert improper↔mixed, integer presentation) into a single aligned concept.

alignment_summary: Across the three codebooks, all skills align one-to-one into four shared concepts with full (3/3) consensus: common-denominator conversion, subtracting with like denominators, rewriting mixed/whole numbers into subtractable forms, and regrouping/borrowing with final simplification. No expert introduced additional unique skills beyond these four, and every skill_id maps cleanly to exactly one concept.
